pages.title: Talking to an Elder
text: Every tribe's camp has an **Elder**, and once you are a Guest they will talk to you. Right-click one and a conversation opens: what they say on the left, what you can say back as buttons.
Trading is one of the things you can ask for. Strangers only get a few gruff words and a hint about the hearth, so bring an offering first (see [Tribes and standing](standing)).
What the Elder offers changes with what you have done: requests, their story, and once you have finished it, a warmer welcome.
On the tribe's [festival day](living_march) the Elder also invites you to the feast.

pages.title: Requests
text: Ask an Elder **"Is there work I can do?"** and they give you one of the tribe's requests. Each tribe has three open on any given day, and they change with the days, so if today's does not suit you, come back tomorrow.

You hold **one request per tribe** at a time. Once you have finished **three** in a day, across every tribe, the Elders hand out no new work until tomorrow. Work you already hold can still be handed in.

Finish it and tell the Elder **"I've done what you asked."** Each pays **8 to 16** standing, and every **third** finished request for a tribe pays a **Tribe Mark** on top, long before you reach Voice.
The Codex keeps track for you: every tribe's page ends with their open request and how far along it is.

pages.title: What they ask
text: - **Fetch**: bring what they prize, such as their March crop. Carry it when you tell the Elder.
- **Deliver**: bring two bowls of their own [dish](tribe_dishes).
- **Hunt**: turn back six of the dark's creatures within **48 blocks** of their hearth. The kill must be your own.
- **Rite**: perform any rite at a brazier or pedestal within 48 blocks of their hearth.

- **Build**: raise **Walls** of size 3 or more within 48 blocks of their hearth, marked with Builder's Chalk, and hold that chalk when you tell the Elder. Build them of worked blocks such as planks, bricks or cobblestone: raw stone, earth, sand, terracotta, ice and the March's own ground do not count. A build counts **once**: walls already handed in to that tribe will not pay again.

pages.title: Their story
text: Ask **"Tell me your story"** and the Elder begins a longer road: **seven steps**, one tribe at a time, that lean on everything else you do with them. Become their Friend, bring the one thing they prize, hunt near their fires, perform a rite in their camp, bring their dish, and at the end go where they send you.

The last step is a **trial**: each tribe's country keeps a guardian, and the tribe wants it faced. The Loom-stitchers' trial is The Unsung itself; the other eight wait at their grounds, told in [The guardians](guardians). Fall in the fight and the story simply waits. A guardian left alone for half a minute goes back to sleep unbeaten, and its altar can be called again straight away.
Face the guardian only once the Elder sends you. A guardian beaten earlier does not count for the story.

pages.title: The nine relics
text: Finish the story and the Elder hands you the tribe's **relic**: a small, unique thing that grants that tribe's [boon](tribe_boons) whenever it is in your inventory, whatever your standing, and marks you for good in their eyes.
One for each tribe, each the end of a story and the start of nine agreeing again.
